title: A Wreck for the Rivergate
premise: Hazel Thornbury flies medicine and mail into the Rivergate interior, keeping her head down to outrun a debt and a past she'd rather forget. When prospector Elias Vann dies in her care, he trades her a hand-drawn map to a lost claim in exchange for one promise: see it registered before the concession permits expire at monsoon's end. Pursued by the mining syndicate's enforcer, who wants the map and the silence of everyone who's seen it, Hazel teams up with Junie Okonkwo, a riverboat engineer with her own reasons to distrust the law. Together they run the flooded waterways in a leaking boat, racing the rising water, the expiring permits, and the men on their tail. In the end Hazel registers the claim in Elias's daughter's name rather than her own, pays her debt with the truth instead of money, and chooses a life where she can finally be seen.
about_author: Hazel Dunmore spent six years as a float-plane dispatcher in northern bush country, where she collected the river stories that fuel her fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who survive by their wits and are haunted by what survival cost them.

chapters.title: Freight and Rumors
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A routine supply flight into Rivergate establishes her world: the debt she owes, the compass she never explains, and her careful habit of being forgettable. She overhears that concession permits expire when the monsoon ends. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: The Man in the Alder Flats
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On an emergency medevac she finds prospector Elias Vann gut-shot beside his burned camp, muttering about a claim no one believes exists. She splints him into her plane against her better judgment. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: A Promise for a Map
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Dying in her cabin, Elias trades her an oilcloth-wrapped map for a sworn promise: register the claim before the permits lapse, in the name of his estranged daughter, Mara Vann. He dies at dawn. Emotional beat: grief braided with dread as she realizes what she's inherited.

chapters.title: Visitors Who Don't Knock
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Syndicate enforcer Corliss Hale arrives asking polite questions about Elias's last flight. Hazel lies well but not perfectly; Hale notices the fresh grave behind her cabin. Emotional beat: cold fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Engineer at Pier Nine
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie Okonkwo, blacklisted from legitimate work after testifying against the syndicate, agrees to run Hazel downriver in her patched boat the Kestrel—for a share and for spite. Emotional beat: two guarded women recognizing a fellow survivor.

chapters.title: Downstream Before Dark
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The first leg of the river journey goes smoothly until they spot a syndicate seaplane shadowing them. Hazel reads the map by lantern light: the claim lies three days up the flooded Sable Fork. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into pursuit.

chapters.title: What the Compass Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A quiet night scene: Junie asks about the compass, and Hazel admits it belonged to her father, who died flying contraband to pay the same syndicate—the source of her debt. Emotional beat: confession as first real trust.

chapters.title: The Leaking Kestrel
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The boat's hull opens on submerged fencing; they beach at a drowned trading post to patch it while the monsoon intensifies. Hale's launch passes within shouting distance. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension under tarpaulin rain.

chapters.title: Trading Post Ghosts
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Among the ruined post's papers Hazel finds Elias's old registration filings—rejected twice on syndicate pressure—and letters to Mara he never sent. Emotional beat: righteous anger replacing fear; the stakes become justice, not gold.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. A syndicate toll station blocks the Sable Fork junction. Junie talks them through with forged manifests while Hazel hides the map inside the compass casing. Emotional beat: nerve-shredding performance, then giddy relief.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Flash flood forces them miles off-course; they lose a day of fuel and half their supplies rescuing a stranded family, who repay them with local knowledge of a back channel. Emotional beat: kindness as strategy and grace.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: Hale's POV (first antagonist chapter). Hale interrogates the toll keeper, learns the Kestrel's route, and radios ahead to burn the back channel's waystation. His own history with Elias is hinted—he was there the night the camp burned. Emotional beat: patient menace.

chapters.title: The Burned Waystation
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They find the waystation still smoking and realize someone sold their route. Suspicion strains the alliance until Junie confesses she radioed her old union contact—not the syndicate. Emotional beat: betrayal feared, loyalty proven.

chapters.title: Portage Through the Devil's Teeth
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The rapids above the fork force a brutal overland portage of engine and supplies through leech-haunted swamp. Hazel sprains her wrist; Junie carries double. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into partnership.

chapters.title: The Claim
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They reach the marker cairn: a working vein, assay tags in Elias's hand, and evidence the syndicate jumped his original stake years ago. The permit clock has four days left. Emotional beat: awe and vindication shadowed by how little time remains.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Cairn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hale's men arrive at dawn. In a running fight through the fog, Junie is shot in the shoulder and Hazel takes a hostage—Hale himself—when she realizes he fears exposure of the burned camp more than losing the map. Emotional beat: terror weaponized into leverage.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Flood
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. With the river rising and Hale bound in the boat's hold, Hazel negotiates: his testimony about the jumped claim in exchange for walking away. He refuses—until she reveals she has Elias's letters naming him at the fire. Emotional beat: power inverted; justice outside the law begins.

chapters.title: The Long Run Downriver
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The desperate final run: patched hull, wounded pilot-passenger, prisoner aboard, monsoon at full fury. They shoot the last rapids as the syndicate seaplane loses the weather and turns back. Emotional beat: white-knuckle momentum, grim humor between the women.

chapters.title: Registry Office, Last Day
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Permits expire at noon. Hale, released but honor-bound by the bargain, corroborates the filing against his own employers. The clerk stamps the claim in Mara Vann's name with minutes to spare. Emotional beat: trembling triumph.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel tracks down Mara Vann, hands her the map, the letters, and the deed, and tells her the whole truth—including her father's death. Mara's grief and gratitude land hard. Emotional beat: promise kept; weight transferred.

chapters.title: Settling Accounts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hazel publicly discloses the syndicate's coercion, voiding her father's debt; Hale disappears rather than testify further, and Junie's blacklist quietly lifts. The two women repair the Kestrel together. Emotional beat: reckoning without revenge; costs acknowledged.

chapters.title: A Wreck for the Rivergate
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Epilogue: months later, Hazel flies the mail again—but now her name is on the registry books, her compass points toward home, and Junie waves from Pier Nine. The title's meaning lands: the wrecked boat, the wrecked past, both salvaged. Emotional beat: earned peace, open horizon.
